name: Queensland clay-cliff "rock-look" sandbag wall (ICM transcript) vs. Scarborough Cliffs Stabilisation Project (candidate site)
place: Thread A (ICM transcript): unnamed site, Queensland. Thread B (candidate): Scarborough, Redcliffe Peninsula, Moreton Bay Region, Queensland

lat_lon.value: not found (precise coordinates not published for either thread)

year_built.value: Thread A: not stated. Thread B (candidate site): construction completed March 2020
year_built.note: Thread A site is unidentified; Scarborough is the best-available published candidate but its material description (shotcrete) directly contradicts the transcript's '5-ton sandbags' claim

type_materials: MISMATCH FLAGGED: ICM's own conference talk (Thread A, unnamed site) describes a rock-look wall actually built from 5-ton sandbags. The only published ICM Queensland clay-cliff project (Thread B, Scarborough) is documented in two independent sources (company case study + peer-reviewed ICCE paper) as a GFRP-reinforced shotcrete wall with soil nails; a rock armour revetment was considered and rejected; sandbags are not mentioned in either Scarborough source.

dimensions.thread_a_sandbags: not stated (no bag count, wall length, or footprint given)

designer: ICM (International Coastal Management), Gold Coast, Australia — Thread B jointly with Moreton Bay Regional Council (MBRC) engineers; paper authors Sam King, Martin Mulcahy, Bobbie Corbett, L. Angus Jackson (ICM)
contractor: Thread A: not stated. Thread B: Australian Marine & Civil Pty Ltd (tender awarded by MBRC)

cost.note: not disclosed in any source found for either thread

financed_by: Thread A: not stated (implied local-government/community-requested). Thread B: Moreton Bay Regional Council (MBRC), which initiated the project
purpose: Cliff erosion protection at a popular, walkable public beach; both threads describe the same twin goal of stopping erosion while preserving public amenity/walkability, though the chosen material differs
current_status: Thread A: implied success, refurbished once in kind (sandbags again) at community request, no failure described. Thread B: post-construction monitoring through Feb 2022 storm events reports the shotcrete wall performing well and successfully preventing further cliff retreat; monitoring ongoing

outcome_summary.thread_a: No numeric outcome data given in transcript (no longevity figure, no storm-survival count)
outcome_summary.thread_b: Shotcrete wall reported intact and effective after Dec 2020 and Feb 2022 storm events; no ecological follow-up study found beyond a design-stage claim that the textured surface would support mollusc habitat
